verdicts.strongest_argument: This finding is a transcription of a public aggregator page that is stored in the capture. docs/5004436bd35a22d6c9aff2fa2f7924b1190feeff.txt is stockanalysis.com/stocks/saic/forecast/ fetched 2026-08-29T13:21:09Z and it prints, in the plainest possible form, 'Price Target: $121.5 (-3.54%)', 'Analyst Consensus: Hold', the month-by-month recommendation trend showing 2 Strong Buy / 8 Hold / 1 Strong Sell unchanged since March, the $93-$137 target range, and 'EPS This Year 10.18 / Revenue This Year 7.19B'. Every number in the claim is on a public page displaying it as of the last session before the print. Restating published consensus is the top of the scale. The magnitudes are also small once checked against the company's own numbers, which are equally published in the corpus: docs/ba0dd5634ed0f6fd2a668eee184d8dd96e842dbd.txt at 2026-06-01T11:25:27Z carries 'SAIC raises FY27 adjusted EPS view to $9.90-$10.10 from $9.50-$9.70, Consensus $9.63. Backs FY27 revenue view $7B-$7.2B, consensus $7.15B.' Street $10.18 against a $10.10 guide top is an 0.8% gap; $7.19bn against a $7.2bn guide top is 0.1%. Calling that 'above the top of guidance' is arithmetically true and economically trivial, and the CFO's own published framing (govconwire, 2026-06-01) is that revenue will 'trend toward or slightly above the midpoint'. Finally, the bear case is on the tape with a name and a number: Goldman Sachs Sell, target raised to $96 on 2026-06-11, 24% below spot, in the same stored document. And the finding's own tape evidence -- the 08-28 rejection of the 52-week high, -2.33% on 848k against a 407k average -- is an argument that the market was already de-risking into the print.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The composition of the Q1 beat is published in the corpus in the very document the finding cites, and the finding concedes as much. docs/5cbc2f27afc1e9226bcbc8076c1167815b3896ee.txt is the govconwire piece of 2026-06-01, stored in full, and it states the $12 million venture-IPO gain, the 60 basis points of EBITDA margin it contributed, that this 'prompt[ed] SAIC to raise its full-year margin guidance to a range of 10.1 percent to 10.3 percent', the timing of materials, the RITS extension, organic growth of 0.5 percent and the CFO's statement that revenue guidance stays unchanged with a trend 'toward or slightly above the midpoint'. That is not a footnote -- it is the trade-press lead paragraph, three months old, on a name eleven analysts cover with a 10-Q filed the same day. The $200m RITS headwind is likewise published in the corpus at 2026-06-01T19:03:16Z, and so is the cautionary framing: the captured headline at 2026-06-01T17:40:49Z reads 'SAIC Stock Rockets After Upbeat Q1 - CFO Flags Caution On Uncertainties In A Dynamic Environment', which is the opposite of a wire that hid the caveats. Goldman's Sell at $96 was reiterated ten days after this release. What survives is only the forecast that Q2 guidance goes unchanged, and the finding's own tape point -- $92.68 on 05-12 to $125.96 on 08-28 -- is 'the market re-rated on a print whose contents were fully published', which cuts both ways.

The wire headline itself pairs the beat with the CFO's caution, and the same file publishes the $200m RITS recompete headwind for FY27.
Stored call summary carrying management's cautious framing, the recompete roll-offs and the portfolio review -- the finding's own cross-check is a captured, published document.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json 2026-06-01/02 gap: the entire +10.44% reaction and the subsequent re-rating happened after the Q1 release, i.e. after the one-off was disclosed in the same release. The stock then spent three months between 100.60 and 128.96 with realised vol of only 23.1% annualised -- an orderly re-rating on public information, not a squeeze on a hidden fact. verdicts.what_would_change_it: A corpus item showing sell-side FY27 models that had *not* stripped the $12m gain -- for instance a broker note carrying an EBITDA margin at the raised guide with the one-off still in the base -- would be a genuine analytical gap and take this to 40-50.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I concede the capture's twelve stored bodies say nothing about this 8-K -- I grepped the doc directory for '2.03', 'credit agreement', 'term loan', 'revolv' and 'financing' and the only hit is an unrelated options target zone. But three things hold it down. First, the filing is not hidden: it is a full public 8-K, accepted 2026-08-19T20:03:23Z, and it is *in this corpus* as an index row in filings.json and snapshots/20260829T131326Z.json, so it was reachable by anyone including every one of the eleven covering analysts. Second, it is routine for this issuer: the same index shows 8-Ks with the identical item triple 1.01, 2.03, 9.01 accepted 2025-09-25T20:36:07Z and 2025-10-01T20:06:03Z, eleven months earlier, which is the signature of scheduled credit-facility housekeeping rather than a structural action. Third, timing and size. SAIC's fiscal Q2 FY27 ended 2026-07-31; an agreement event-dated 2026-08-14 falls outside the quarter being reported and was already disclosed twelve days before the print, so it delivers no new information at the print itself. The two Form 3s of 2026-08-20 and the item-5.02 8-K of 2026-08-10 are officer-onboarding paperwork at a company that has filed four 5.02 items since October 2025, and none of it is sized. The bars show nothing: the 8-K landed after the close on 08-19 (that day closed 128.71) and 08-20 was 126.29, -1.9% on 446k against a 407k average -- inside normal noise for a 23% realised-vol name, and the stock made a new 52-week high six sessions later. The finding says itself it cannot be signed; I agree, and an unsigned unread filing that was public before the print is not an edge.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The agreement itself was publicly filed twelve days before the print; the corpus index carries it, so it was reachable to the market even though no captured body discusses it.
Two earlier 8-Ks with the identical 1.01/2.03/9.01 item triple, establishing that this issuer files such items as routine facility housekeeping.

verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the 8-K body showed new incremental debt of a size that matters against a company generating >$600m of free cash flow -- say an acquisition financing rather than a facility amendment -- and it were event-dated inside the reported quarter, this would drop below 15.

interactions: Findings 0 and 1 are one mechanism ('the bar is too high going into this print') resting on overlapping documents: #0's independence cross-check is docs/10d350826fb56a102779a47a99c2ab25f199dbed.txt, the same Q1 call summary that supports #1, and both consume the same 2026-06-01 guidance-raise event and the same 2026-08-28 distribution bar. The hunter flags the cluster. Finding 2 is independent of them but points the other way in one respect: it argues the market has not looked at SAIC's filings, while #0 and #1 rest on the market having looked closely enough to raise eight price targets. Only the larger residual of 0/1 should be counted, and 2 is close to noise.
